subtitle: When the Lion of Kalinga Rode North

panels.shot: epic split-composition, wide shot with two opposing hosts fading into each other
panels.action: On one side Narasimhadeva I stands atop a war elephant under the coastal Odisha sky; on the other, Tughril Tughan Khan grips his sword before the foggy banks of the Ganga, the lands of Rarh, Gauda and Varendra stretching between them.

dialogue.text: In the 1240s, as frontier raids scarred Odisha’s borders, Gajapati Narasimhadeva I rode north toward Lakhnauti, forcing Bengal’s Mamluk governor Tughril Tughan Khan to decide: retreat behind walls, or meet the lion in the open.

i18n.hi: १२४० के दशक में सीमा-छापेमारी से ओड़िशा झुलस रहा था, तब गजपति नरसिंहदेव प्रथम लाखनौती की ओर उत्तर चढ़े, forcing तुगरिल तुघान ख़ाँ को चुनना पड़ा: किले में छुपे या मैदान में शेर का सामना करे।

panels.shot: wide aerial shot over the Bay of Bengal coast, slow push-in
panels.action: A sweeping view of Odisha’s coast: temple spires rise behind fortified towns, and watch-fires burn along the frontier roads as news of northern raids reaches the Eastern Ganga court.

dialogue.text: For years, riders from the north probed Odisha’s borders, testing villages and forts, until the Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I faced a choice: build higher walls, or carry the war to Bengal.

i18n.hi: बरसों से उत्तरी सवार गाँवों और किलों को परख रहे थे, जब पूर्वी गंग राजा नरसिंहदेव प्रथम के सामने सवाल उठा: दीवार ऊँची करें या युद्ध खुद बंगाल तक ले जाएँ।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in royal council hall, low-angle on Narasimhadeva
panels.action: In the stone-pillared hall of Cuttack, Narasimhadeva I sits tall on the throne, armored, listening as anxious courtiers gesture to a palm-leaf map showing Rarh, Gauda and Varendra north of Odisha.

dialogue.text: Odishan poets would later praise him as Hamira Mada Mardana, breaker of northern pride, but first there was a real council, real maps, and the hard question of marching into Tughril Tughan Khan’s sphere.

i18n.hi: ओड़िशी कवि बाद में उन्हें ‘हमीरा मद मर्दन’ कहेंगे, उत्तर का घमंड तोड़ने वाला, पर पहले हुई असली सभा, असली नक्शे, और तुगरिल तुघान ख़ाँ के इलाक़े में कूच करने का कठिन फैसला।

panels.shot: close-up on Narasimhadeva’s face, determined, torchlight flicker
panels.action: Torchlight reflects off Narasimhadeva’s eyes as he studies the frontier lines, jaw set, one hand resting on a sword, the faint outline of elephants carved on the throne beside him.

dialogue.speaker: narasimhadeva_i_and_tughril_tughan_khan
dialogue.text: If they ride across our fields, let them first feel the dust of ours upon theirs.

i18n.hi: अगर वो हमारे खेतों से गुज़रें, तो पहले हमारी धूल उनकी आँखों में भरनी चाहिए।

panels.shot: epic wide shot, columns of Odishan elephants and cavalry setting out
panels.action: Long lines of Eastern Ganga war elephants, armored and draped, move north along a forest road, followed by cavalry and foot soldiers carrying banners fluttering in the humid air.

dialogue.text: Between 1242 and 1246, Odishan forces pushed into Rarh, Gauda and Varendra, not as raiders but as a royal campaign, remembered in inscriptions that soon would hail Narasimhadeva as Gajapati, Lord of Elephants.

i18n.hi: १२४२ से १२४६ के बीच ओड़िशी सेनाएँ राढ़, गौड़ और वरेंद्र तक बढ़ीं, लुटेरे नहीं, राज-अभियान बनकर; शिलालेखों में जल्द ही नरसिंहदेव को गजपति, हाथियों के स्वामी के रूप में याद किया गया।

panels.shot: interior shot in Lakhnauti court, focus on Minhaj-us-Siraj writing
panels.action: Within the hall at Lakhnauti, Tughril Tughan Khan listens tensely as messengers report Odishan advances; nearby, the scholar Minhaj-us-Siraj bends over paper, recording the rising alarm.

dialogue.text: In distant Lakhnauti, the Mamluk governor Tughril Tughan Khan heard of the march. His circle, including chronicler Minhaj-us-Siraj, would later preserve Bengal’s fear in the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

i18n.hi: दूर लाखनौती में ममलूक सूबेदार तुगरिल तुघान ख़ाँ को चढ़ाई की खबर मिली। उसके दरबार में, इतिहासकार मिन्हाज-उस-सिराज समेत, ‘तबकात-ए-नासिरी’ में बंगाल की दहशत दर्ज हुई।

panels.shot: medium shot on Tughril Tughan Khan, shadows, tense posture
panels.action: Tughril Tughan Khan stands by a lattice window overlooking the Ganga, brows furrowed, fingers pressing the hilt of his sword as he imagines elephants pressing through the flat eastern plains.

dialogue.speaker: narasimhadeva_i_and_tughril_tughan_khan
dialogue.text: The frontier burns, and now the fire walks on elephant-back toward us.

i18n.hi: सीमाएँ जल रही हैं, और अब आग हाथियों की पीठ पर चलती हुई हमारी ओर आ रही है।

panels.shot: crowded hall shot, ulama and officers around Tughril, high angle
panels.action: Tughril sits surrounded by jurists, commanders and emirs, all debating urgently, hands raised, as a map of Bengal’s districts lies open on a carpet between them.

dialogue.text: Minhaj records panic and calls for jihad in Tughril’s circle, as Bengal’s leaders argued how to resist: hold in Lakhnauti, seek Delhi’s aid, or risk open battle with the Eastern Ganga host.

i18n.hi: मिन्हाज तुगरिल के हलके में फैली घबराहट और जिहाद की पुकार लिखता है; बंगाल के सरदार बहस कर रहे थे: लाखनौती में टिकें, दिल्ली को बुलाएँ या पूर्वी गंग सेना से खुले मैदान में भिड़ें।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of a messenger riding from Lakhnauti, riverbank backdrop
panels.action: A fast rider splashes along the Ganga’s edge, carrying a sealed message toward the north-west, while behind him the walls of Lakhnauti rise under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri speaks of Delhi-linked reinforcements and appeals for help. Yet in these years Bengal’s governor still bore the weight of the defense, as Narasimhadeva’s advance unsettled the province itself.

i18n.hi: तबकात-ए-नासिरी दिल्ली से जुड़ी मदद और फरियादों की बात करता है; पर इन्हीं सालों में सूबे की रक्षा का बोझ अभी भी बंगाल के सूबेदार पर था, जबकि नरसिंहदेव की बढ़त खुद प्रांत को डगमगा रही थी।

panels.shot: wide battlefield establishing shot, Odishan army reaching Bengal plains
panels.action: The Odishan army halts on the open plains of Rarh, dust hanging in the air as elephants lower their trunks and cavalry scan the horizon for signs of Bengal’s forces.

dialogue.text: Vidyadhara’s Ekavali and other Odishan works sing of victories over Yavanabani Ballabha, northern realms, but behind the courtly titles lay real marches, real confrontations in Rarh and Gauda.

i18n.hi: विद्याधर की ‘एकावलि’ और अन्य ओड़िशी ग्रंथ यवनबनी बल्लभ और उत्तर के देसों पर विजय गाते हैं, पर इन दरबारी उपाधियों के पीछे थीं असली चढ़ाइयाँ, असली भिड़ंतें राढ़ और गौड़ में।

panels.shot: medium shot of Narasimhadeva in the field, flanked by generals, low-angle
panels.action: Armored and mounted on his lead elephant, Narasimhadeva confers with generals, gesturing toward distant tree lines and river courses, his banner caught in a sudden wind.

dialogue.text: The Odishan side gives us praise, not detail. We know there was fighting, enough for poets to call Narasimhadeva a terror to northern lords, and for Bengal’s records to remember alarm and loss.

i18n.hi: ओड़िशी पक्ष हमें जयगान देता है, विवरण कम। हम बस इतना देखते हैं कि लड़ाई हुई, इतनी कि कवि नरसिंहदेव को उत्तर के सरदारों का ख़ौफ़ बुलाएँ, और बंगाल के लेख खोफ़ और हानि याद रखें।

panels.shot: tense pre-battle wide shot, two hosts facing off in the distance
panels.action: In the hazy distance, two lines of troops face one another across flat land: Odishan elephants and archers opposite Bengal’s cavalry and footmen, both sides waiting, flags barely stirring.

dialogue.text: The chronicles do not paint each clash. They show the shape of the moment: an Odishan king willing to stand on Bengal’s soil, and a Mamluk governor forced to defend provinces under Delhi’s shadow.

i18n.hi: इतिहास-ग्रंथ हर टक्कर नहीं दिखाते, बस उस घड़ी की शक्ल: एक ओड़िशी राजा जो बंगाल की धरती पर खड़ा होने को तैयार था, और एक ममलूक सूबेदार जो दिल्ली की छाया में सूबों की ढाल बनना मजबूर था।

panels.shot: close-up on Minhaj’s hand writing, ink flowing across paper
panels.action: Minhaj’s hand moves quickly, ink glistening on the page as he notes the troubles, the calls for aid, and the strain upon Bengal in the wake of Narasimhadeva’s incursions.

dialogue.text: From Minhaj we hear of Bengal shaken, of Tughril’s struggles and appeals. From Odisha we hear of triumphs and titles. Between them, the historian must walk carefully, measuring praise against panic.

i18n.hi: मिन्हाज से हमें मिलता है डगमगाता बंगाल, तुगरिल की जद्दोजहद और उसकी पुकारें; ओड़िशा से आता है विजय-गान और ख़िताब। इनके बीच इतिहासकार को सावधानी से चलना पड़ता है, जय और दहशत दोनों तौलते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot in Odishan camp, poets reciting before Narasimhadeva
panels.action: In the evening light of the Odishan war camp, a court poet stands before Narasimhadeva’s tent, reciting verses of Hamira Mada Mardana while warriors listen, faces lit by campfires.

dialogue.text: Odishan literature turns these campaigns into elevated praise: the king as conqueror of foreign realms, the elephants as thunder. The titles tell us that, at least for a time, the offensive felt victorious.

i18n.hi: ओड़िशी साहित्य इन चढ़ाइयों को ऊँचे स्तुति-गीत बना देता है: राजा परदेसी देसों का विजेता, हाथी गरजते बादल। उपाधियाँ बताती हैं कि कम से कम कुछ समय के लिए आक्रमण जीत जैसा लगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of river crossing, Odishan army returning south
panels.action: The Odishan host slowly crosses a broad river on its march south, elephants stepping through shallows, banners drooping, soldiers looking back toward the fading northern horizon.

dialogue.text: What lands Narasimhadeva might have held, or for how long, the record does not securely say. We see only that he could go deep into Bengal’s sphere, then withdraw, leaving a changed memory on both banks.

i18n.hi: नरसिंहदेव ने कौन-कौन सी ज़मीन कितने समय अपने पास रखी, लिखत साफ़ नहीं कहती; हम बस इतना देखते हैं कि वो बंगाल के गहरे हिस्सों तक जा सकते थे, फिर लौट आते, दोनों किनारों की याद बदलकर।

panels.shot: close-up of Kapilash inscription being carved into stone
panels.action: A sculptor’s chisel bites into stone at Kapilash in 1246 CE, carving lines that name Narasimhadeva Gajapati, while a priest and an officer watch the emerging script with quiet satisfaction.

dialogue.text: By 1246, the Kapilash inscription fixes a new title: Gajapati. The campaigns had reshaped his image, from coastal ruler to elephant-lord whose reach had tested the strength of Bengal’s defense.

i18n.hi: १२४६ तक कपिलाश शिलालेख एक नई उपाधि तय करता है: गजपति। इन अभियानों ने उसकी छवि बदल दी — तट के राजा से हाथी-स्वामी, जिसकी पहुँच ने बंगाल की ढाल की ताकत परख ली।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of early Konark Sun Temple under construction
panels.action: On Odisha’s shore, massive stone wheels of the future Sun Temple at Konark are raised by workers, elephants hauling blocks under a blazing sun as priests and architects supervise.

dialogue.text: Later Odishan memory would fold these northern marches into Konark’s story, seeing the great Sun Temple as both devotion and monument to a king who did not hide behind his frontier.

i18n.hi: बाद की ओड़िशी यादें इन उत्तरी चढ़ाइयों को कोणार्क की कथा में पिरो देती हैं, महान सूर्य मंदिर को भक्ति और उस राजा की निशानी मानती हैं जो अपनी सीमा के पीछे नहीं छिपा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Tughril Tughan Khan alone on Lakhnauti ramparts at dusk
panels.action: Tughril Tughan Khan stands on the ramparts of Lakhnauti at dusk, looking out over the quiet plains, his posture heavy with the weight of years spent balancing local threats and distant authority.

dialogue.text: For Tughril, these years were one more test in a troubled governorship, caught between local revolts, frontier offensives and the expectations of the Delhi sultans he served but did not command.

i18n.hi: तुगरिल के लिए ये साल उसके उलझे सूबेदारी के एक और इम्तिहान थे, जहाँ वो स्थानीय बगावतों, सीमा-हमलों और दिल्ली के सुल्तानों की उम्मीदों के बीच फँसा था, जिनकी सेवा तो करता था, हुक्म नहीं चला सकता था।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot, Konark silhouette against the sea and sky
panels.action: The completed Konark Sun Temple stands vast and dark against the glowing sea horizon, stone horses and elephants frozen mid-stride, as waves break below and a lone pilgrim gazes up.

dialogue.text: Narasimhadeva’s march to Lakhnauti shows a frontier king choosing offense over fear; today Konark’s silent stone reminds us that sometimes the strongest wall is the courage to step beyond it.

i18n.hi: नरसिंहदेव की लाखनौती की चढ़ाई दिखाती है कि एक सरहदी राजा ने डर के बदले हमला चुना; आज कोणार्क का मौन पत्थर याद दिलाता है कि कभी-कभी सबसे मजबूत दीवार वही कदम होता है जो उसे पार कर जाए।

subtitle_i18n.hi: जब कलिंग का शेर उत्तर चला
